topic: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
usual_baseline: Buckle fractures are over-treated. Only 7.7% were discharged at the first visit [1476] and 33/84 in another audit [1434]. NICE compliance was 44% combined and 0% at an MIU [1551], with a mean of 1.9 clinic visits [1328]. For forearm fractures, few are manipulated in ED: 9.1% [1446] and 31.94% [1431]. Nationally, BOAST compliance was 63%, consent 38% and post-manipulation NV assessment 35% [1544].
fix_that_works: Parent education, leaflets and emails: 62/64 discharged from ED [1434], and visits fell from 1.9 to 1.2 [1328]. Posters, emails and teaching: DGH compliance 56% to 80% [1551]. An ED pathway with staff education raised ED manipulation from 23/72 to 73/87 [1431]. An SOP using intranasal fentanyl and Entonox cut theatre need from 36.4% to 1.9% [1446].
fix_that_fails: MIU compliance only reached 31%, with rigid immobilisation at 69% [1551]. With a new pathway, first-visit discharge was still only 44.8% and 80.4% still had a back slab [1476]. After pathway change, fracture clinic within 7 days was 49.42% and discharge NV documentation 64.36% [1431].
consultant_advice: Buckle fracture audits against NICE are overdone, and the fix is well known. Audit the MIU and weekend pathways, where gains fail, and check splint stock. Forearm manipulation in ED, with consent, NV checks and clinic within 7 days, is the more useful gap [1544].
